name: Taimaka (HLI, 2024)
summary: Treats children with acute malnutrition in Gombe State, Nigeria. The Happier Lives Institute's estimate of the life-improving wellbeing effects of Taimaka's treatment (WELLBYs per $1,000), rebuilt from the figures in its report.

source.title: Does a well-fed infancy make for a more felicitous life? How treating malnutrition impacts happiness: a charity evaluation of Taimaka
source.license: © Happier Lives Institute; no licence published. Numbers cited as facts with their source.

resources.title: HLI, How treating malnutrition impacts happiness: a charity evaluation of Taimaka (2024)
resources.note: HLI publishes no spreadsheet for this estimate (or only one behind sign-in): the model is built from the inputs and figures stated in the report's text, each quoted on its row. HLI links GiveWell's CMAM model and Taimaka's own cost sheet, not a sheet of its own.

resources.title: HLI, 2025 giving season charities update
resources.note: Rates Taimaka a Promising Charity and restates the figure as 68 WELLBYs per $1,000 (5.43 WELLBYs at $87 a child, which works out at 62); the report's 65.6 is what this model reproduces.

sections.title: HLI's estimates by source of evidence (report Table 5)
sections.explainer: HLI has no randomised trial of treating acute malnutrition with wellbeing outcomes, so it extrapolates from three other bodies of evidence and averages them with equal weight. Each estimate below is HLI's, after its adjustments for validity, generalisability and charity-level factors.

sections.title: Discounting
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not HLI's. HLI counts a year of better wellbeing the same whenever it comes. In our view, later years count less at the discount rate under Your values, as in GiveWell's models; the evaluator view sets the rate to 0, so HLI's figure is unchanged there.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not the evaluator's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: WELLBYs per $1,000: atole protein supplement trial
rows.explainer: From one trial of atole, a protein supplement given to children in Guatemala, followed into adulthood (n = 1,249): 56.84 WELLBYs of direct effect, times HLI's validity (0.26), generalisability (0.41) and charity-level (0.88) adjustments, is 5.23 WELLBYs per child treated, at $87 a child.

rows.label: WELLBYs per $1,000: natural experiments on famine
rows.explainer: From two natural experiments on the long-run scarring of famine (n = 34,724): 11.37 WELLBYs of direct effect, times 0.75, 0.75 and 0.88, is 5.63 WELLBYs per child at $87.

rows.label: WELLBYs per $1,000: small-quantity nutrient supplements (IQ pathway)
rows.explainer: From a meta-analysis of 13 trials of small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (n = 23,588), through their effect on IQ: 17.29 WELLBYs, times 0.43, 0.98 and 0.88, is 6.31 WELLBYs per child at $87. HLI also works out a social-emotional pathway (22.2 per $1,000) but gives it no weight, taking the higher pathway as a floor.

rows.label: WELLBYs per $1,000 (life-improving effects)
rows.explainer: HLI weighs the three sources equally: "we estimate that the life-improving WELLBYs per $1k (WBp1k) generated by Taimaka to be 65.6" (section 5). HLI counts only life-improving effects in this figure; it estimates the lives saved could add about 65 WELLBYs per $1,000 for those who value saving lives highly, and grief averted 3 more, but treats both as bonus effects that depend on unsettled philosophical choices. GiveWell's model of Taimaka (on this site) values the lives saved.

rows.label: Discount rate on future wellbeing
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). HLI doesn't discount, so the evaluator view pins it at 0.

rows.label: Years the wellbeing effect lasts

source.title: HLI report
source.quote: a wellbeing effect of approximately between 0.09 to 0.46 standard deviations (SDs) per person that lasts 62 years

rows.explainer: HLI's duration for the wellbeing effect of treatment in early childhood. We spread HLI's WELLBYs evenly over these years from now, which is generous to the near years (the effect HLI measures shows up in adulthood).

rows.label: Discount factor for benefits spread evenly over those years
rows.explainer: The present value of an equal benefit each year over the years above, starting now, as a share of the undiscounted total: 1 at a 0% rate, lower the longer the benefit lasts.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs where staff deliver the help themselves (treatment, counselling, coaching, outreach): staff pay is about half the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits often earn somewhat less than in comparable jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: WELLBYs per dollar
rows.explainer: The figure per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
